definition: Whether training discovers trajectories the policy would not already produce, and across 10 sources a quantity the archive treats as poorly measured rather than well understood. The corpus's central methodological point is that the usual proxies do not measure it: token entropy cannot distinguish exploration from learning wrong trajectories -- one source calls a high-entropy condition 'entropy without exploration' -- and pass@k describes inference-time behaviour after training rather than what training discovered. The replacement several sources converge on is a paired count against a reference run: a prompt is rescued if the method produces a correct rollout where the baseline produced none, and lost in the opposite case, with degenerate and incorrect rollouts counted alongside. Its authors are explicit about the limits -- defined relative to a baseline it is a comparative diagnostic rather than an absolute measure, and it counts a rescue on one correct rollout without asking whether that rollout's reasoning was sound. The substantive findings are that verifiable-reward training reduces exploration on both modalities measured, though the controlled comparison is against a distilled policy trained on the same data rather than against the base model, and that concentrating exploration has a real if small cost on shorter horizons -- one transfer result loses on the benchmark where its host method was strongest.

evidence.note: Estimates what a continuous latent thought is worth by freezing the context after it and averaging the rewards of several answers sampled from that fixed context, then credits latent positions with the resulting thought-level advantage and answer positions with the ordinary group-relative one.
evidence.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

evidence.note: Inserts a stage before RL in which the model extracts textual lessons from its own successful and failed rollouts, filters them by measured marginal utility on a held-out probe set, and distills the surviving pool into its own weights — so that GRPO starts from a policy that fails all-eight-samples less often.
evidence.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

evidence.note: Treats a policy's per-problem failure probability as a random variable over the problem distribution and shows that REINFORCE, pass@K training and MaxRL each optimize a single moment of it, then proposes minimizing the first T moments jointly — which is exactly minimizing the expected truncated number of rollouts needed to reach a first success.
evidence.title: Beyond the Mean: Multi-Moment Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Builds prefix trees of semantically equivalent reasoning statements and measures how RLVR changes a model's preference between branches, finding the entropy collapse is not stylistic — the collapse is stronger for semantically distinct continuations than for syntactic variants of the same statement.
evidence.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?

evidence.note: Shows that GRPO's per-completion uniformity is frequency-skewed once credit is aggregated by solution structure — a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass proportional to how often it is sampled — and rebalances it by a rarity exponent over a partition built from deterministic cue signatures rather than a judge model.
evidence.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO

evidence.note: Turns table-to-report generation into Monte Carlo tree search over partial reports, scored by a reward that verifies every numerical claim by generating and executing SQL against the source table rather than by asking a judge — and keeps that search reward strictly separate from the benchmark's own evaluator to avoid a reward-hacking loop.
evidence.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Table-to-Multimodal Report Generation

evidence.note: A GRPO variant for flow-based generative models that replaces SDE training rollouts with an ODE step plus a Langevin correction, aligning training samples with the deterministic sampler used at test time.
evidence.title: LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction

evidence.note: Replaces the monotonic zoom-in that tool-using video agents follow once they pick a region with a policy that self-checks each tool observation and can switch regions, and trains it with turn-level credit applied multiplicatively -- reweighting the trajectory advantage's magnitude while preserving its sign -- rather than additively.
evidence.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

evidence.note: Explores in weight space rather than token space during RLVR by sampling policies from a variational posterior at rollout time, and introduces a training-time exploration metric -- how often a method produces a correct rollout on a prompt where GRPO produced none -- because entropy and pass@k cannot tell exploration from degeneration.
evidence.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

evidence.note: Shows that selecting the most confident rollout can be worse than picking at random, because uniformly high confidence signals a failure to explore rather than a well-supported answer, and replaces maximisation with a temporal criterion that penalises early certainty while requiring late certainty.
evidence.title: Consilience for Verifier-Free Test-Time Scaling

name: exploration
